jobs.description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation's top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

Overview

As part of the GPSU program, we are seeking an AI & Data Science Intern to support GuidePoint Security's Northeast region. In this role, you will work with the NE AI and AppSec teams as part of the NE DevSecOps team, contributing to the evaluation and governance infrastructure that supports GuidePoint's agentic AI harnesses. This is a hands-on, practitioner-mentored role focused on defining and running evals, collecting and analyzing telemetry, tuning model performance, and building an internal governance pipeline for AI harness outputs. Prior professional experience is not required, but a data-oriented mindset and curiosity about applied AI systems are essential.

Currently enrolled, or recently graduated with a degree or substantial coursework in data science, statistics, computer science, engineering, or a related field is required. You will contribute to live AI systems that are in active use across the organization, working alongside experienced engineers to improve harness reliability and prevent output drift and performance regression over time. You will also participate in limited client-facing engagements under mentorship, observing how AI capabilities are communicated and demonstrated in a professional services context.

Responsibilities

Evaluation & Performance

Define and implement evaluation frameworks to measure the accuracy, reliability, and consistency of agentic AI harnesses
Design and run structured evals against harness outputs to detect regressions, output drift, and behavioral degradation over time
Build and maintain benchmark datasets and ground-truth corpora used to evaluate harness quality
Analyze eval results, identify failure modes, and collaborate with the NE AI and AppSec teams to drive iterative improvements
Research and apply prompt evaluation techniques and LLM benchmarking methodologies relevant to security-specific harnesses
Telemetry, Tuning & Governance

Instrument agentic harnesses with telemetry to capture latency, token usage, error rates, and output quality signals
Analyze telemetry data to identify patterns, surface anomalies, and generate actionable insights for harness tuning
Support model and prompt tuning efforts based on eval and telemetry findings, documenting changes and measuring their impact
Contribute to building an internal AI governance pipeline: defining standards, logging outputs, flagging quality issues, and maintaining an audit trail for harness behavior
Document governance processes, eval methodologies, and tuning decisions in a repeatable, version-controlled format

Qualifications

Currently enrolled, or recently graduated with a degree or substantial coursework in data science, statistics, computer science, engineering, or a related field (required)
Proficiency or strong interest in Python, with exposure to data manipulation libraries (pandas, numpy) or LLM APIs
Genuine curiosity about large language models, agentic systems, and how AI performs (and fails) in applied contexts
Strong analytical and written communication skills, with an ability to translate data findings into clear, actionable observations
Technical aptitude and comfort working with ambiguity in a fast-moving, practitioner-led environment
Eastern/Central time zone, preferred

Internship Details and Expectations

This is a part-time, remote paid internship ($20/hr) that runs for 12 weeks, with potential for full-time employment at the conclusion of the internship. Interns are expected to:

Be physically located within the United States during the entire duration of the internship
Work 25-29hrs/wk Monday-Friday supporting the Eastern Time Zone
Have a personal computing device and access to high-speed internet during working hours

This position is not available for candidates living in the following states: Alaska, California, Hawaii, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming.

GuidePoint Security is a rapidly growing, profitable, privately-held value added reseller that focuses exclusively on Information Security. Since its inception in 2011, GuidePoint has grown to over 1,300 employees, established strategic partnerships with leading security vendors, and serves as a trusted advisor to more than 6,200 customers.

Firmly-defined core values drive all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to the company's success and establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. This is a unique and rare opportunity to grow your career along with one of the fastest growing companies in the nation.

About Figure

Figure (NASDAQ: FIGR) is transforming capital markets through blockchain. We’re proving that blockchain isn’t just theory - it’s powering real products used by hundreds of thousands of consumers and institutions.

By combining blockchain’s transparency and efficiency with AI-driven automation, we’ve reimagined how loans are originated, funded, and traded in secondary markets. From faster processing times to lower costs and reduced bias, our technology is helping borrowers, investors, and financial institutions achieve better outcomes.

Together with our 170+ partners, we’ve originated over $22 billion in home equity loans (HELOCs) on our blockchain-native platform, making Figure the largest non-bank provider of home equity financing in the U.S. Figure’s ecosystem also includes YLDS, an SEC-registered yield-bearing stablecoin that operates as a tokenized money market fund, and several other products and platforms that are reshaping consumer finance and capital markets.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Most Innovative Fintech Startups in 2025 and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies in Finance and Personal Finance.

About The Role

At Figure, we’re redefining what’s possible at the intersection of finance and technology. Fresh off our IPO, we are building the next generation of financial infrastructure, transforming how capital moves, how credit is assessed, and how customers experience financial products. Our data team sits at the heart of that transformation, serving as the analytical engine that powers the entire business. From architecting the data models that drive risk and capital allocation to delivering the reporting and insights that guide growth strategy and operational excellence, we ensure every department has the intelligence needed to win.

As a Senior Data Analyst, you will be a vital driver of our growth and product evolution, partnering closely with Marketing, Product Management, and Engineering to optimize the borrower journey. Your work will directly influence how we acquire customers, the efficiency of our loan application funnel, and the long-term value of our customer base.

You will bridge the gap between user behavior and business strategy, combining analytical rigor with product intuition to help leaders understand the "how" and "why" behind the customer experience. While your primary focus is on the front-end growth engine, you are a generalist at heart—capable of architecting data models that serve the entire organization’s need for clear, actionable intelligence from top-of-funnel to capital allocation.

What You’ll Do

Data Modeling & Architecture: Design and implement robust data models that transform fragmented marketing spend and application event logs into structured, "gold-standard" datasets. You will ensure our product and acquisition data is clean, organized, and optimized for cross-functional use.
Funnel Optimization: Build and maintain scalable frameworks to monitor the loan application funnel—identifying friction points, drop-off behaviors, and opportunities to improve conversion from lead to funded loan.
Technical Impact: Elevate our analytics toolkit by writing high-performance BigQuery SQL and designing intuitive Tableau dashboards that empower stakeholders to track KPIs like CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost), Approval Rates, and Origination Volume in real-time.
Experimental Design: Partner with Product and Marketing to design, execute, and analyze A/B tests, ensuring we make evidence-based decisions on everything from landing page optimization to credit offer presentation.
Cross-Functional Insight: Act as the analytical backbone for the business, translating complex user behaviors into repeatable, automated insights that drive measurable growth and product-market fit.

3–5+ years of experience using data to drive measurable business impact, specifically within Growth, Product Analytics, or Marketing Science.
Deep proficiency in SQL (preferably BigQuery); you are an expert at handling complex joins and window functions to reconstruct user journeys across marketing touchpoints and loan applications.
Advanced Data Modeling: Proven ability to design and maintain structured datasets (star schemas, dbt models) that turn messy clickstream and CRM data into reliable tables for the entire business.
Expertise with Tableau: You don’t just report data; you build intuitive dashboards that help managers visualize cohort performance, attribution models, and funnel velocity.
Statistical Depth: Strong grasp of statistical concepts like survival analysis (to model time-to-repayment or time-to-next-loan), causal inference, and significance testing.
Fintech/Lending Context: Understanding of the lending lifecycle—from initial acquisition through underwriting to funding—and how product changes impact portfolio quality.
Communication: Clear, confident ability to translate complex data trends into actionable stories for both technical teams and executive leadership.
Adaptability: A generalist mindset—you are comfortable navigating the ambiguity of a fast-moving environment and can apply your analytical toolkit to solve problems across different business domains.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) are limited to pre-analytical and supportive functions only and may not read, record, result, verify, or interpret any laboratory test. They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

Responsibilities

The Laboratory Assistant will follow the guidelines set by CLIA, and the California Business and Professions Code Sections 1212 and 1269. Unlicensed laboratory personnel (“aides”) are limited to pre-analytical and supportive functions only and may not read, record, result, verify, or interpret any laboratory test. They may not perform any test involving the quantitative measurement of specimens or reagents, conduct mathematical calculations related to test results, perform instrument calibration, or monitor or interpret quality control data used to assess test system performance. Unlicensed personnel shall not participate in any phase of testing that involves result generation, interpretation, verification, or reporting.

All duties must be performed under the direct and constant supervision of a physician and surgeon or a licensed laboratory professional, as defined by California regulations.

Unlicensed laboratory personnel may perform approved activities including specimen collection (patient preparation, labeling, handling, processing, preservation, transportation, and storage), assisting licensed personnel, preparing and storing reagents and culture media, assisting with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (without calibration or performance verification), and supporting quality control procedures (without interpretation of results). Specimen collection involving venipuncture or skin puncture may only be performed if the individual holds appropriate California phlebotomy certification (e.g., CPT I or CPT II) or other qualifying license, as required by law.

This individual: 1) Performs computer entry, filing, telephone communication, and other clerical duties. 2) Demonstrates professional telephone etiquette and greets patients and visitors courteously. 3) Possesses effective verbal and written communication skills. 4) Demonstrates knowledge of laboratory test terminology. 5) Demonstrates knowledge of phlebotomy practices; performs venipuncture or skin puncture only if appropriately certified per California law. 6) Processes specimens across laboratory departments including pathology, microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry, and blood bank limited to pre-analytical activities (e.g., specimen handling and centrifugation only in immunohematology). 7) Prepares and processes specimens for reference laboratories. 8) Stocks and orders routine supplies. 9) Maintains cleanliness and organization of storage areas, equipment, centrifuges, and collection sites. 10) Processes and places specimens on laboratory instruments for automated analysis only, without performing test setup, calibration, validation, or result review. 11) With documented training, may assist with preventive maintenance and troubleshooting (excluding calibration and performance verification), assist in quality control procedures (without interpreting results), and perform permitted microbiology support tasks such as primary culture inoculation, slide staining, and subculturing. 12) Performs additional duties assigned by department leadership, including clerical support, communication tasks, specimen transport, and interdepartmental deliveries. 13) Assists Pathology with pre-analytical and clerical tasks only, including specimen receipt, accessioning, labeling, transport, and storage, under direct supervision and within regulatory limitations. 14) Functions as a runner to support laboratory workflow and specimen movement as needed.

Qualifications

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, TRAINING

HS Diploma or equivalent required.
Active California Certified Phlebotomy Technician I or II license required for individuals performing phlebotomy.
Current BCLS (AHA) certificate upon hire and maintain current preferred.
BLS certification within forty-five days of hire and maintained current, according to hospital requirement.
Minimum of 1 year clinical laboratory experience performing similar job functions preferred.
